Barns around the state are ready to get back to business following the holidays with everyone having a full schedule of sales for the first business week of 2022. 12/13/2021:
Compared to last week, feeders under 750 lbs. sold steady to 5.00 higher, heavier weights sold mostly steady. Heavier weight cattle not as abundant now, as many especially the high quality ones have already been marketed at this point. The last full marketing week of the year did
see very strong prices for the lighter weights though as prices continue to climb. The number of sales over the next two weeks will be very limited as barns take either one or two weeks off for the holidays. The weather continues to be quite odd for mid- December, southern Missouri did see some heavy rains and flash flooding late in the week. The northwest corner of the state caught some high winds and had some power outages but was spared most of the extreme damage that was seen into Iowa and north. Records highs were set again a few days last week, before cold came over the weekend, although another warm up is expected by Christmas. Surprisingly cattle seem to be doing pretty well with all the temperature swings and most producers are reporting not a lot of health issues with calves they have in the weaning pens despite the crazy weather. Negotiated feedlot sales were light this week, as the next two will be short holiday weeks and packers have most of the inventory they require just need enough to set a negotiated price for formula reasons as much as anything. The Missouri Stocker Formula consist of 8411 head with a weighted average weight of 546.28 lbs. and a price value of 174.67, 2.19 higher than last week.

Supply moderate with demand moderate for weaned and worked cattle, but light to moderate for unweaned bawling calves. Temperature swings have started up, making buyers more conscious of programs and body condition. Wheat is coming up and the warm days with rain made it shoot up last week. Cattle going on the wheat and rye has been sought after and bringing a premium, if they were the right kind. October’s cattle on feed report was released on Friday, showing bullish data. On feed was at 98.6 percent of last year’s inventory at 11,550,000 head. The average industry guess was at 99.3 percent. This was the second highest inventory for October 1, since the series began in 1996. Placements in feedlots came in at 97.1 percent, with the average industry guess at 101.2 percent. Placements on feed during September totaled 2,163,000 head. Marketings totaled 1,789,000 head, 96.9 percent of last year’s inventory. The average industry guess was at 97.3 percent. Friday’s estimated slaughter report showed 661,000 head of cattle for the week, bringing the year-to-date slaughter at 26,938,000 head. This is 822,000 head more than where we were a year ago. In feedlot trade, live cash prices stayed mostly steady at 124.00 and dressed mostly steady at 196.00. There was about 70,000 head negotiated cash and about 48,000 head negotiated grid. Monday’s Missouri Stocker Formula consisted of 4279 head with a weighted average weight of 547.27 lbs and a price value of 163.12, 0.62 lower than last week.

08/23/2021: Compared to last week, feeder steers and heifers sold steady to 5.00 higher. The supply of feeders was light as extreme heat once again affected what is normally a light time for marketing cattle anyway. Heat indices climbed into the triple digits for several days and it isn’t a dry heat in Missouri. Demand was moderate to good. Buyers are discounting the unweaned bawling calves that won’t adjust to a new environment or dry dust very well and these discounts will continue to get larger each week until after frost and temperatures stabilize in another month and a half or so.  Heavier weight load lots of yearlings on the other hand get buyers on the phones and closer to the edges of their seats. A couple of highlights this week was a pot load of steers at Kingsville Livestock Auction weighting 839 lbs. and sold for 164.00, another pot load at New Cambria Livestock Market weighting 925 lbs. sold for 155.25.  Dry conditions have several farmers finding pasture and hay crop damage from army worms. Infestations in Missouri haven’t been as devastating as some other states but there has been several finding populations high enough to require spraying. What is catching many off guard is populations are being found much farther north than is typical catching many producers off guard.  Boxed beef cutouts were a little calmer this week, Choice closed on Friday at 345.34, up 0.28 and select at 315.52, 3.01 lower than the previous week. Negotiated feedlot sales as of the last report on Friday afternoon totaled just under 52k head. It is likely more took place after hours and just didn’t get turned in to make the report. Record breaking winter weather keep every reported action in the state dark except three special replacement cow sales held on Friday and Saturday. Boxed beef cutouts closed higher for the week. Choice closed on Friday at 239.23, up 6.86 and select at 227.90, up 6.97 compared to the previous week. Feedlot sales for the week as of the last report on Friday had volume of just over 65K head, live sales were mostly 113.00-115.00 and dressed sales mostly 180.00-182.00.  Slaughter numbers were lighter this week once again due to winter weather though out the nation. The monthly cattle on feed report was published on Friday and was considered bearish as analyst missed placement numbers. On feed numbers were reported at 101.5 percent, marketings 94.3, and placements at 103.2 which was 3.5 percent above the average pre report numbers.  Due to there was no feeder cattle auctions the Missouri Stocker Formula was not available.
02/08/2021: Compared to last week, feeders sold uneven with most of the mid-weight cattle selling within 2.00 on either side of even.  Markets were highly affected by weather this week with many barns all out cancelling and those that had sales had very light offerings. The coldest weather of the year so far quickly froze up mud and about everything else. Snow, wind and record setting temperatures over the weekend made caring for livestock a difficult job. According to weather service this is the longest continuous cold streak of weather since 1983 and on track to flirt with the record set in 1936. Many sales have already cancelled into this week as well, due to poor travel conditions and dangerous wind chills.  Boxed beef cutouts were mixed for the week, choice closed at 232.37, down 2.21 and select 220.93, up 0.14 from the previous week. Feedlots sales as of the last report on Friday afternoon showed negotiated volume right at 73K head and its possible some took place after hours as well.  Live sales were reported mostly 113.00-115.00 and dressed sales mostly at 180.00 although some higher late sales will likely pull the average just over 180.00.  The Missouri Stocker Formula consists of 2015 head, again highly affected by weather, with a weighted average weight of 551.93 and a price value of 155.81, down 1.35 from the previous week.
02/01/2021: Compared to last week, steers under 650 lbs. sold 3.00 to 5.00 higher with spots of 6.00-8.00 higher. Steers over 650 lbs. sold steady to 3.00 higher. Heifers sold mostly 2.00 to 4.00 higher with some 500-600 lbs. heifers up to 6.00 higher. The supply of feeders was moderate and demand was moderate to good with grazing type cattle finding the most interest. Although muddy there was no additional moisture to deal with until very late week and into the weekend. A very strong dose of artic air arrived which will finally freeze the mud up for a while.  Although single digits with below zero wind chills are not enjoyable and can be a real pain trying to run feed equipment the cold dry air is much better for feeding and adding weight to cattle than the wet mud. Boxed beef cutout values slowed from the dramatic weekly climbs over the last several weeks. Choice closed on Friday at 234.58, up 0.63 and select closed at 220.79, down 1.91 for the week. As of the last report on Friday afternoon negotiated feedlot sales totaled just under 87k head. Lives sales were reported mostly 112.00-115.00 and dressed sales from 178.00-180.00 with a few loads up to 184.00. The Missouri Stocker Formula consist of 6195 head with a weighted average weight of 558.12 lbs. and a price value of 157.16, 1.42 higher than last Monday.
01/25/2021: Compared to last week, feeder steers and heifers sold steady to 2.00 higher. The supply of feeders was light to moderate as weather was less than favorable for transporting livestock. Heavy rain fall early in the week, then mid-week snow fell followed by more rains. Flash flooding was a problem in some areas but mud is becoming a much larger problem. Wet cold mud is not the type of weather that producers want trying to keep calves looking good and gaining weight prior to marketing. Several barns in the northern part of the state canceled sales early due to the forecast of snow. Demand for feeders is moderate to good. Buyers are eagerly trying to fill orders for summer grazers before the best ones are gone and supplies get tight. Boxed beef cutouts continue to climb. Choice closed Friday at 233.95 up 11.13 and select closed at 222.70 up 9.36 compared to the previous week. Feedlot sales as of the last report on Friday afternoon totaled just under 55K head of negotiated sales, however it is likely there was more business late Friday but just how much will not be known till mid-morning Monday. Sales that were reported however were much higher as feedlot managers dug in hard trying to get a little big slice of the pie. Live sales were mostly 110.00-113.00 and dressed sales were reported from mostly 174.00-178.00 with some up to 181.00.  The semi-annual cattle inventory report was released late Friday afternoon. On the national level most numbers were fairly in line with estimates. The one exception was the number of beef heifers being kept for replacements which came in at 100% of the previous year which was 2% above estimates. Missouri maintained the 3rd spot in the nation for beef cows that have calved but that number was down 2% for a total of 2.035 million head. The 2020 calf crop was estimated at 1.91 million head also down 2% from the previous year. The Missouri Stocker Formula consisted of 3953 head with a weighted average weight of 549.97 lbs. with a price value of 155.73 up 4.22 compared to last Monday.
01/18/2021: Compared to last week feeders under 600 lbs. sold unevenly steady to 5.00 lower, feeders over 600 lbs. sold steady to 3.00 higher, with the 600-750 lbs. steers seeing the most strength after a few weeks of being under a lot of pressure.  The supply of feeders was moderate, much lower than the last couple of weeks, but that is typical as new marketing year progresses. Demand was moderate to good, already reports of some buyers collecting grazing cattle for summer which comes as no surprise as some expect supplies to tighten in the coming months. Locally individual market trends were very wide this week with instances anywhere from 10.00 lower to other locations seeing spots of up to 10.00 higher. A lot of factors played into these wide ranges, lighter offerings, quality differences, and with all that went on this week markets definitely saw different effects simply by the day of the week.  Early week saw a lot of outside influences and uncertainty mostly due to political reasons with the unknowns of what might happen with the presidential transfer of power. Then mid-week markets were more focused on Ag related issues. Weather and harvest in South America caused grain prices tumble. On the futures markets corn closed the week down 0.30-0.34 cents and beans closed 1.00-1.05 lower which made feed cost outlooks much better. On Friday the nearby bean contract lost .58 ½ cents which was the largest one day loss since July 2016. Cattle futures rallied with feeder contracts closing the week 2.68 to 8.33 higher and live cattle 0.50 to 4.32 higher, which pushed the much talked about Apr to 122.52 an eleven month high. The monthly COF report was somewhat of a heartbreaker however, as pre report estimates expected the report to be quite bullish. That failed to materialize though as on feed numbers were reported at 100 percent, placements at 101 well above the average estimate of 97 and even the top of the estimate range of 93-100, and marketings were reported at 101 percent. Although in the short term the report failed to provide numbers that were hoped for it did provide some hope for the coming months as no one believes these continued high numbers can hold out into summer. Next Friday the semi-annual inventory will be released which should support decreased supplies unless USDA finds a lot of stock that most farmers just do not believe exist. Boxed beef cutouts climbed sharply higher, choice closed Friday at 222.82 up 9.90 and select closed at 213.34 up 10.26 both compared to the previous week. Feedlot volume for the week as of the last report on Friday afternoon showed a volume of just over 88k head of negotiated sales. Live sales were reported mostly from 108.00-111.00 and dressed mostly 170.00-173.00. The Missouri Stocker Formula consisted of 6949 head with a weighted average of 556.61 lbs. and a price value of 151.51, down 0.67 from last Monday.
01/11/2021: Compared to last week, feeder steers and heifers sold 2.00 to 5.00 lower with some spots of 5.00 to 8.00 lower, expect steers under 550 lbs. sold which steady to 3.00 higher. Although not as large as last week the supply was still heavy with many auctions having big runs once again. Demand was good but at lower price levels. Grain prices spiked higher on Tuesday following the monthly WASDE and final USDA production numbers for 2020.  As of Friday’s report corn prices have passed the 5.00 mark at nearly all elevators in the state and over 5.50 at some of the larger terminal and barge locations. That is near a dollar per bushel higher than this same week last year. Cattle prices however are much the opposite compared to the same week last year 525 lbs. steers are 6.00 per cwt lower and 775 lbs. steers are about 11.00 per cwt lower.  Slaughter steers out of the feedlots are currently about 15.00 per cwt lower on live sales and 25.00 lower dressed.  Boxed beef cutouts ended the week higher with choice closing on Friday at 212.92 up 6.12 and select at 203.08 up 6.39. Feedlot sales were lower this week as of Friday afternoon about 95K head of negotiated sales were reported for the week with live sales mostly 108.00-111.00 and dressed mostly 172.00-174.00. Cattle slaughter for the week was estimated at 651,000 head which is a decent chain pace. The Missouri Stocker Formula consisted of 9976 head with a weighted average of 558.00 lbs. and a price value of 152.18, down 1.50 from last Monday.
01/04/2021: Compared to very light receipts over the last two weeks, feeders under 600 lbs. sold 1.00 to 5.00 higher, with some 4 weights seeing sharply higher tops on some thinner fleshed high quality groups. Feeders over 600 lbs. sold mostly 2.00 to 5.00 lower.  Typically the largest volume week of the year and the first week of 2021 set a pretty high bar with a very heavy supply of cattle covering the entire weight spectrum. Weather conditions over all were pretty favorable for transporting cattle and auctions ran late into the night at most locations. Some farmers are dealing with a little bit of mud in a few areas of the state mostly in the south, as temperatures aren’t staying cold enough to keep the ground frozen. Demand was moderate to good, even though prices were lower on heavier weight cattle buyers still fought hard and bidding was active just lower price levels and many reporters noted that markets held whatever levels they had established though out the long auctions. Light weight grazing type calves with many more days left found the best demand as there is a lot more time for them to offer opportunities for profit.  The steer/heifer spread is about 15.00 on the lighter weights and 10.00 on the heavier which is much more in line with what is generally expected. Feedlot sales for the week as of Friday were just under 73k prices were mixed with live sales ranged from 109.00-112.50 with an average price late Thursday of 111.54 which would be slightly higher. Dressed sales ranged from 174.00 all the way up to 180.00 on a few lots, the average as of late Thursday was 176.10 which would also be a touch higher. Friday’s sales were a bit lower and likely going to pull those averages down to about even with the previous week.  Boxed beef cutouts were also mixed choice closed Friday at 206.80 down 3.15 and select closed 196.69 up 1.01.  Friday’s Missouri Stocker Formula consists of 10,436 head with a weighted average weight of 560.95 lbs. and a price value of 153.69, 1.07 higher than last Monday.
